text:
Maria: ran a quick bring-up of r-infer/llama-3-q8 this morning with function-calling enabled. seeing ~18% parser failures on our structured-output eval set :grimacing:
Jordan: ouch. are those true malformed JSON or schema mismatches?
Maria: mostly malformed JSON. common patterns: trailing commas, unescaped backslashes, and occasionally extra text before the object. sometimes the `message` key contains a markdown block + code fence.
Sam: do we still have the same system/prompt steering we used in the earlier tests? maybe q8 quant changes tokenization weirdness.
Maria: same system message as prod. compared to fp16 baseline, q8 has slightly higher hallucination rate on labels. but the parse failures are disproportionately higher.
Nitya: can you paste a few raw outputs (sanitized)?
Maria: sure, sample 1:
```
{"id":"1234","intent":"create_event",}
```
sample 2 (weird case):
```
Some text\n{"id": "1235", "intent": "update", "entities": [
  {"type":"date","value":"2026-04-01"}
]}
```
Jordan: wow, second one has a prefix. our parser chokes because we pass to JSON.parse directly.
Oliver: two quick mitigation ideas: 1) post-output sanitizer to strip leading non-json text and trim trailing commas; 2) instruct the model to output only JSON via function_call and add a strict system message + one-shot example. both together might reduce failures.
Sam: for (1) we already tried a regex cleanup but it failed on nested edge cases. maybe use a lightweight tolerant parser that can recover common issues?
Nitya: eval plan: run a small batch (1k samples) across fp16, q8, q4 to compare parser failure rate, schema-violation rate, and core metric (intent accuracy). also collect top-k failure patterns.
Maria: started that job — linking results when ready. initial 200 samples: fp16 parser failures 2%, q8 16%, q4 12%. intent accuracy: fp16 93%, q8 90%, q4 91%.
eval-bot: job 2026-04-02-09:14 finished — attached summary CSV (uploaded to /mnt/evals/q8-parse-run1.csv).
Jordan: do we allow retries? i.e., if parsing fails, do a deterministic retry with: system message override + `output_format: JSON_ONLY` + temperature 0?
Maria: we have a retry flow in the runtime but it's disabled for function-calling endpoints currently because of at-least-once semantics concerns. enabling it might duplicate side effects for tools.
Oliver: suggestion: create a sandboxed retry mode for evals (no side effects) and for production expose a conditional retry that only runs for read-only/toolless calls. also consider a backoff/backtracking policy: on parse failure, ask the model to "fix" the last output by returning only the corrected JSON. example low-cost retry payload:
```
System: You are a strict JSON generator. Reply with only a single JSON object matching this schema: {"id":"string","intent":"string","entities":"array"}
User: The model output was: <PASTE_RAW_OUTPUT>. Please return only the corrected JSON.
```
Nitya: can we also incorporate schema validation at the function-call level? Redwood platform could validate the function-call response against the JSON schema and mark it failed before returning to the app, triggering a retry or fallback.
Sam: that sounds good. two implementation options: a) runtime-level schema validation + automatic retry with altered prompt; b) SDK-friendly helper that attempts to coerce/repair then returns both repaired JSON and a confidence flag.
Maria: for the short term I'm leaning to (b) because it's faster to ship and avoids server-side semantic duplication. long term we should do (a) with metrics & opt-in policies.
Jordan: for metrics, we need per-model breakdowns (fp16/q8/q4), per-deployment (hosted/dedicated), and per-route. add test ids so we can correlate examples to prompts.
Oliver: also observed that some failures are due to function-calling: the model sometimes emits `function_call` with name and args string that itself is an escaped JSON string. like `{"name":"create","arguments":"{\"id\":\"x\"}"}` which our parser interprets wrongly. we should normalize by double-parsing `arguments` when necessary and flag if it was nested.
Maria: good catch. putting that on the repair heuristics list.
Nitya: follow-ups: 1) Maria to share full CSV + representative raw outputs; 2) Sam to prototype SDK repair helper; 3) Oliver to draft runtime schema-validation RFC (opt-in); 4) Jordan to enumerate retry semantics for function-calls (idempotency rules).
Maria: timeline: I'll push CSV + a short failure taxonomy by EOD.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline notice — new eval VPC snapshots will be available in 30m.
Sam: one more thought — quantization may change token boundaries, so adding a short example-based correctness check (1-2 shot) inside system prompt that shows exact JSON tokens might anchor generation. cheap to try.
Maria: agreed; will A/B that in next run. thanks all :thumbsup:
